items.title: How much smaller is Git's storage than manual copies, as the project changes?
items.description: Grounded in the unit's own numbers: a manual copy stores the entire project again on every save, while Git's content-addressed storage only pays for what actually changed since the last commit (plus one full copy up front). Drag the number of saves/commits and how much of the project changes each time, and watch the gap between the two strategies.

params.name: changedPercent
params.label: Share of project changed per save

items.compute: const changedFraction = params.changedPercent / 100; const manualCopyKB = params.numCommits * params.projectSizeKB; const gitStorageKB = params.numCommits <= 0 ? 0 : params.projectSizeKB + (params.numCommits - 1) * params.projectSizeKB * changedFraction; return { manualCopyKB: Math.round(manualCopyKB), gitStorageKB: Math.round(gitStorageKB) };
